Transform data in growthcleanr format into wide structure for BMI calculation

Source: R/utils.R
longwide.Rd

longwide transforms data from long to wide format. Ideal for transforming output from growthcleanr::cleangrowth() into a format suitable for growthcleanr::ext_bmiz().

Usage

longwide(
  long_df,
  id = "id",
  subjid = "subjid",
  sex = "sex",
  agedays = "agedays",
  param = "param",
  measurement = "measurement",
  gcr_result = "exclude",
  include_all = FALSE,
  inclusion_types = c("Include"),
  extra_cols = NULL,
  keep_unmatched_data = FALSE,
  sex_coding = .gc_default_sex_coding,
  param_coding = NULL
)

Arguments

long_df

A data frame (or data.table) to be transformed. Expects columns: id, subjid, sex, agedays, param, measurement, and an exclusion column from cleangrowth() (named "exclude" by default; the cleangrowth() output data.table can be passed directly).

id

name of observation ID column

subjid

name of subject ID column

sex

name of sex descriptor column

agedays

name of age (in days) descriptor column

param

name of parameter column to identify each type of measurement

measurement

name of measurement column containing the actual measurement data

gcr_result

name of column of results from growthcleanr::cleangrowth(). Defaults to "exclude", the name of the exclusion column in cleangrowth() output. If your exclusion column has a different name, pass it explicitly. If the named column is missing and the default "exclude" was used, the error says so and suggests gcr_result = "gcr_result" (the column name 2.x scripts used).

include_all

Determines whether the function keeps all exclusion codes. If TRUE, all exclusion types are kept and the inclusion_types argument is ignored. Defaults to FALSE.

inclusion_types

Vector indicating which exclusion codes from the cleaning algorithm should be included in the data, given that include_all is FALSE. For all options, see growthcleanr::cleangrowth(). Defaults to c("Include"). A value that is not a growthcleanr version 3 exclusion code (for example the 2.x code "Exclude-Carried-Forward") matches no rows, so longwide() warns and points to the code mapping in vignette("experienced-start-here").

extra_cols

Vector of additional columns to include in the output. If a column C1 differs on agedays matched height and weight values, then include separate ht_C1 and wt_C1 columns as well as a match_C1 column that gives booleans indicating where ht_C1 and wt_C1 are the same. If the agedays matched height and weight columns are identical, then only include a single version of C1. Defaults to empty vector (not keeping any additional columns).

keep_unmatched_data

boolean indicating whether to keep height/weight observations that do not have a matching weight/height on that day

sex_coding

Named list with elements male and female giving the sex codes used in long_df, exactly as for cleangrowth(). The default recognizes the same codes cleangrowth() does (0/1, m/M, f/F, b/g, male/female, boy/girl; case- and whitespace-insensitive). If you passed a sex_coding to cleangrowth(), pass the same one here. Sex is output as M or F, which ext_bmiz() reads directly. As in cleangrowth(), with the default coding longwide() stops if sex has only 1s and 2s, and gives a prominent warning if every value is 1 across more than one subject; passing sex_coding removes both. A warning is also given if any retained row's sex is missing or not recognized (its sex becomes NA, so ext_bmiz() cannot compute BMI z-scores for it).

param_coding

Optional named list mapping your parameter labels to growthcleanr's canonical parameters, exactly as for cleangrowth() (e.g. list(WEIGHTKG = "wt", HEIGHTCM = "ht")); pass the same one you gave cleangrowth(). Parameters are read the same way cleangrowth() reads them: imperial values (HEIGHTIN, LENGTHIN, WEIGHTLBS) are converted to cm/kg and LENGTHCM is treated as height, so ht and wt are always metric. Head circumference rows are not used; rows with an unrecognized parameter are dropped with a warning.

Value

Returns a data frame transformed from long to wide. Includes only values flagged with indicated inclusion types. Potentially includes additional columns if arguments are passed to extra_cols. For each subject, heights without corresponding weights for a given age (and vice versa) will be dropped unless keep_unmatched_data is set to TRUE. The subject and age columns keep the names you passed as subjid and agedays (for example patid); the other columns are agey, agem, sex (recoded to M or F), ht_id, wt_id, wt (kg), and ht (cm). If no rows are kept, a data frame with these columns and no rows is returned.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Run on a small subset of given data
df <- syngrowth[syngrowth$subjid %in% unique(syngrowth$subjid)[1:5], ]
gc_out <- cleangrowth(df)
#> [14:18:16] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 5 subjects, 93 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (93 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 45 included (80.4%), 11 excluded (19.6%)
#>   Height      : 32 included (86.5%), 5 excluded (13.5%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************
df$exclude <- gc_out$exclude[match(df$id, gc_out$id)]

# Convert to wide format (default gcr_result = "exclude")
wide_df <- longwide(df)

# Include all inclusion types
wide_df <- longwide(df, include_all = TRUE)

# Specify which exclusion codes to retain (default `exclude` column uses
# the Summary codes; pass `exclude_detail = TRUE` to cleangrowth() and use
# `gcr_result = "exclude_detailed"` for the step-level Detailed codes)
wide_df <- longwide(df, inclusion_types = c("Include", "Exclude-CF"))
# }
